To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heterotrimeric motor kinesin-1 is required for the ciliary transport of the photoreceptor membrane receptor opsin.
the movement of opin, the membrane receptor for the phototransduction cascade, in ciliated cells is comparable to that of IFT proteins, and that this movement requires the heterotrimeric motor KIF3A.
the ciliary transport of rod photoreceptor opsin is mediated by heterotrimer KIF3A.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transport of the visual receptor opsin along the plasma membrane of the ciliary compartment.
the molecular mechanism of photoreceptor cell function.
the mechanisms of ciliary membrane transport, and we provide evidence that the highly conserved heterotrimeic kinesin 2 is required for normal transport of op sin along the ciliary membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the movement of opins in the ciliary axonemes is driven by heterotrimeric kinesin- 2.
the heterotrimeric Kif3A/B/C kinesin is required for the transport of rod opsin in cilia of photoreceptor and non-photoreceptor cells.
the heterotrimeric KIF3 complex (kinesin-2), the most conserved of the IFT motors, is required for the anterograde transport of opsin in cilia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
heterotrimeric KIF3A/KIF3B is a major motor protein for ciliary membrane transport.
the heterotrimeric KIF3A/KIF3B complex is required for the ciliary transport of opsin.
heterotrimeric KIF3A is required to transport ciliary opsin in rod photoreceptor outer segments.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have provided evidence that the conserved intraflagella transport (IFT) system of cilia is involved in the transport of opsin in the outer segment, a structure that is unique to photoreceptor cells.
we show for the first time that heterotrimeric KIF3A is involved in the transport of a membrane protein, opsin, in the ciliary compartment of a nonphototransducing cell.

the ciliary transport of rod photoreceptor opsin, as well as that of other ciliary membrane receptors and channels, is likely driven by the conserved heterotetrameric kinesin-1 and the conserved heterodimeric kinesins, such as heterotrimeric KIF3A/KIF3B and KIF17.
